title: Periodic meter sampler skew causing per-route billing gaps
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Observed undercounting of request tokens for certain per-route meter buckets when the periodic sampling worker runs on boundaries of variable-length windows. A subset of customers reported lower-than-expected usage on invoices; internal reconciliation shows gaps in the route-level sampled histogram used by the billing pipeline. Affects hosted API routes with heavy short-burst traffic and routes behind route-alias normalization.

Symptoms:
- Per-route token counts intermittently drop to zero for 30-90s windows while per-org totals look correct.
- Billing pipeline ingests sampled histograms and extrapolates volume; sampled histograms with zero buckets caused ~10-20% undercharges for affected intervals.
- Issue appears correlated with the periodic sampler tick aligning with the internal window rotation logic and an off-by-one in the in-memory circular buffer index when route alias mapping changes during the tick.
reproduction_steps: 1) Create two test routes R-A and R-Alias where R-Alias resolves to R-A via route alias mapping.
2) Send high-frequency short requests (~50ms) to R-Alias for 2 minutes, with bursts every 10s.
3) Force the periodic sampler to run at 60s boundaries (simulate production sampler timing) and rotate windows at the same time.
4) Inspect the sampler output histograms for R-A and R-Alias. Expect to see empty/zeroed buckets in the per-route histogram while org-level counts and raw request logs show requests were processed.
5) Run the billing extrapolation on the sampled histogram and compare to raw token logs to reproduce undercount magnitude.
impact_summary: Medium customer impact: 7 customer tenants observed billing undercharges during March 2026 pilot windows (estimated revenue delta $2.3k over affected intervals). Functional user-facing impact is low (no request rejections), but financial reconciliation and trust are impacted. Internal alerting did not fire because org-level counters were sane; only per-route sampled histograms were affected.
timeline: 2026-02-25: Issue filed after finance spotted billing reconciliation deltas for 5 customers.
2026-02-26: Eng on-call triaged; initial repro built in staging reproducing zeroed per-route histogram buckets.
2026-03-01: Root-cause hypothesis added - window rotation race when alias mappings change during sampler tick.
2026-03-04: Hotfix deployed to sampler (feature-flagged) that adds coarse-grained lock around window rotation; immediate mitigation applied for producer clusters.
2026-03-08: Backfill job implemented to re-extrapolate missing intervals for affected customers; finance notified and refunds scheduled where appropriate.
2026-03-12: In-progress: full code fix under review, extended unit and integration tests being added, rollout plan prepared.
investigation_notes: Sampler code uses 8-window circular buffer (idx 0..7) rotated every 15s for 2m aggregations. Alias normalization calls can mutate route->bucket mapping asynchronously.

Race observed when alias normalization triggered remap while sampler rotated: the remap zeroed the new route bucket but the sampler wrote to the old index; result: histogram bucket reference dropped (garbage) and later rotation produced zero snapshot.
Heap memory and GC traces show no leaks; root issue is index remap + pointer stale reference, not loss of events in ingestion pipeline.
Reconstructed traces from request logs show tokens accounted at org-level aggregator before sampling stage; discrepancy introduced during histogram snapshot capture.
Staging repro yields consistent 12-18% undercount when rotation aligned with alias update; out-of-phase rotations show normal counts.
root_cause: An index remapping race between the periodic histogram sampler and the route-alias normalization path. When alias mappings change during a sampler tick the circular buffer index used to snapshot per-route histograms could point at a bucket that had just been zeroed or re-associated, producing an empty snapshot even though events were recorded earlier in the pipeline.
mitigation: Deployed feature-flagged coarse lock around window rotation to prevent concurrent remap during snapshot capture (hotfix).
Ran a one-off backfill re-extrapolation job for affected customers to correct invoices for the impacted intervals.
Enabled a temporary alert that compares per-route sampled extrapolation vs raw org-level token rate and fires when discrepancy > 5% for two consecutive samples.
rollout_plan: Canary the full fix (lockless pointer-swap strategy) to 10% of producer clusters for 24h, validate via reconciliation job and sampler discrepancy alert, then 100% rollout over 48h. If discrepancy reappears revert to hotfix lock and investigate further.
next_steps: Merge code fix with added deterministic unit tests for alias remap during rotation (PR review in progress).
Add integration test that runs sampler rotation + alias updates at boundary timings to catch regressions.
Improve sampling telemetry: capture a lightweight per-window checksum to detect zeroed snapshots in future without full replays.
Coordinate with Finance on final invoice adjustments and a customer communications draft.
acceptance_criteria: Unit + integration tests covering alias remap during sampler rotation pass in CI.
Staging canary shows sampler discrepancy alert false negatives < 0.5% over 24h.
Backfill job re-extrapolation results validated against raw logs for a random sample of 3 customers.
Code reviewed and signed off by runtime and billing owners.
notes: Finance prefers issuing credits for the pilot customers and running reconciliations weekly until the fix is fully validated.
Consider retiring sampled-histogram extrapolation for small tenants and switch to deterministic counting when tenant size < threshold to avoid sampler-induced revenue drift.
